messages.subject: Coda-like functionality in Stan
parts:
We're designing an object stan::mcmc::samples that
will hold samples across multiple chains like Coda
in R. Jiqiang, Daniel and I have been putting some
thought into this and met today to come up with this
design.

There are some lingering questions we can take up at
the next Stan meeting.

This is checked into the end of stan/TO-DO.txt,
but I've also included it below.

(TO-DO.txt could use some spring cleaning -- I'll
go through and do that over the weekend.)

- Bob


Coda-like Object Design
========================

One thing we didn't discuss -- ESS for pow(X,2),
basically to test second moment estimation.
I think these should be available just about everywhere
the first order stuff is available.

QUESTIONS
---------
What to do if M[k] != M[k']?
- cut to minimum?
- generalize R-hat, ESS calcs

Is there bias in stopping when you hit
an ESS estimate of 40? What's expected
number of samples and pattern of variance?

Do we store the warmup samples in here?

R2WinBUGS does what when giving data to Coda?
Does it throw away first half? Should we?
-- We'll just use the post-burnin samples.


Should we do DIC or something like it?
Need:
deviance(theta) = - 2 log p(y|theta) + C
deviance(mean(theta))
How to get deviance(mean(theta))? In fact, how to
get the log likelihood -- there's not a term for it
in Stan -- need to know what data is and exclude terms
that only depend on the prior! (Maybe we could reverse
the templating in our function calls for probability
functions?)

Randomize samples across iterations? Why?

Keep # burnin samples?


K: # chains
M[k]: # samples
N: # total params
L: # named params

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Coda-like functionality in Stan
parts: Some replies:

On May 11, 2012, at 4:26 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:


Is there bias in stopping when you hit
an ESS estimate of 40?
We're not monitoring this every iteration, are we?
Does it throw away first half?  Should we?
There should be an argument to the function saying what fraction to throw away as warmup.  1/2 can be the default for now.

-- We'll just use the post-burnin samples.


Should we do DIC or something like it?
If we do anything, I think we should do waic, not dic.  I still need to run these experiments.

Need:
  deviance(theta) = - 2 log p(y|theta) + C
  deviance(mean(theta))
How to get deviance(mean(theta))?  In fact, how to
get the log likelihood -- there's not a term for it
in Stan -- need to know what data is and exclude terms
that only depend on the prior!  (Maybe we could reverse
the templating in our function calls for probability
functions?)

Randomize samples across iterations?  Why?

The samples can be saved in order.  But there should be a way to extract parameters.  For example, if the stan object is "foo", then something like sims(foo)$theta would pull out the simulations of theta.  In this case I think it would be good to mix and scramble the chains.  I would like "everyday inference" (as opposed to convergence monitoring) to scramble the chains so that it's not about the MCMC, it's about the inference.  Of course the user should also be able to access the unscrambled chains directly if desired.  The order of scrambling can be saved in the stan object (i.e., we don't want it to rescramble each time sims() is called; it's important that the sims for different parameters go with each other).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Coda-like functionality in Stan
parts:
On 5/11/12 7:02 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> Some replies:
>
> On May 11, 2012, at 4:26 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>>
>>
>> Is there bias in stopping when you hit
>> an ESS estimate of 40?
>
> We're not monitoring this every iteration, are we?

Of course not! That would be craziness.

We only need to do ESS once unless we use it
as a convergence criterion (see below).

I just realized how little context I gave everyone
who wasn't at the meeting! I was hoping to discuss
some of these things at the next Stan meeting as they
may take more bandwidth.

Right now, the initial plan's to set the number
of iterations like in R2WinBUGS.

The output will go into this object we're designing,
which will be exposed to R (and Python or MATLAB).

>> Does it throw away first half? Should we?
>
> There should be an argument to the function saying what fraction to throw away as warmup. 1/2 can be the default for now.

That's how the command line already works and
how the R code will work, too.

Then we probably want a rerun command that'll
be similarly configurable (with some way of counting
from restart).

Then we can set the combo up to auto-run like in R2jags.
We could either use max R-hat or minimum ESS or both.

Something like doubling or growing by 50% the number
of samples each time until convergence seems reasonble.

We could update a plot of R-hat histograms each time
we checked.

The question, though, was whether the Coda-like object
stores the warmup samples or not. R2WinBUGS (or
Coda) I believe throw away the initial warmup
samples -- at least you don't get them back when
you attach or in the traceplots. But they do
seem to keep track of how many were thrown away
so they can index their graphs that way. I don't
think that'll be necessary -- the caller will know.

>> -- We'll just use the post-burnin samples.
>>
>>
>> Should we do DIC or something like it?
>
> If we do anything, I think we should do waic, not dic. I still need to run these experiments.

Either way, we have to somehow specify how the
likelihoods get computed and stores.

>> Need:
>> deviance(theta) = - 2 log p(y|theta) + C
>> deviance(mean(theta))
>> How to get deviance(mean(theta))? In fact, how to
>> get the log likelihood -- there's not a term for it
>> in Stan -- need to know what data is and exclude terms
>> that only depend on the prior! (Maybe we could reverse
>> the templating in our function calls for probability
>> functions?)
>>
>> Randomize samples across iterations? Why?

> The samples can be saved in order.

In fact, they have to be. Otherwise, we can't compute
R-hat, ESS, etc.

> But there should be a way to extract parameters. For example, if the stan object is
> "foo", then something like sims(foo)$theta would pull out the simulations of theta.

Yes, we're on that. We've been burning up the Rcpp mailing
list getting help on how to access the dimensions so if
theta is an A x B matrix and there are K chains of M samples
each, then you can get back theta as an array either with
dims equal to c(A,B,M,K) if you want chain IDs or c(A,B,M*K)
if you want the chains merged.

> In this case I think it would be
> good to mix and scramble the chains. I would like "everyday inference" (as opposed to convergence monitoring) to
> scramble the chains so that it's not about the MCMC, it's about the inference. Of course the user should also be able to
> access the unscrambled chains directly if desired. The order of scrambling can be saved in the stan object (i.e., we
> don't want it to rescramble each time sims() is called;

When does "everyday inference" change if you use ordered
samples? If they start running autocorrelation on the
output (where it will matter), they're going down the
wrong road anyway. We couldn't imagine a case where it'd
matter when we were thinking about it this afternoon which
is why the question's in there.

> it's important that the sims for different parameters go with
> each other).

Good point about keeping the rows (samples for all params)
together -- we'd give a rather misleading view of parameter
correlation in the posterior if we didn't! We can either keep
a random seed and re-run Knuth's permutation algorithm with
the same seed, or we could actually store the permutation of
1:K and just reapply it each time (presumably what you did in
R given how easy that is with their indexing).

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Coda-like functionality in Stan
parts:
Yes, I think the stan object should save the warmup samples along with various HMC tuning parameters as they are tuned during the run. It's cheap to save them and they could be useful for diagnostics.
A
